I'm also barely sleeping because I lie awake replaying work and wake up at 3 AM, which has made me so irritable that I've been snapping at my husband and teammates over minor things.\n\nDoctor: How much is this worrying and the physical tension affecting your day-to-day life at work, at home, or in relationships?\n\nPatient: It is having a massive impact on every part of my life. For me, it's more of a constant, background level of spinning worry and physical tension that just stays with me throughout the entire day.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had sudden panic attacks—brief episodes where fear spikes quickly and you get symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, chest tightness, or feeling like something terrible is about to happen?\n\nPatient: No, I've never experienced sudden panic attacks like that, with a racing heart or shortness of breath. My anxiety is much more of a constant, ongoing state of background worry and physical tension that just stays with me all day.\n\nDoctor: Have you also been feeling down, losing interest or pleasure in things, or having any thoughts that life isn’t worth living?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel depressed, and I've never had any thoughts that life isn't worth living. My anxiety is much more of a constant, lingering background tension and non-stop worrying that stays with me all day, rather than sudden peaks that fade.\n\nDoctor: When your worry is at its worst, do you also get symptoms like muscle tension, feeling restless or keyed up, fatigue, trouble concentrating, or irritability most days?\n\nPatient: Yes, I definitely experience those symptoms on most days.
